On 4 December 1977 Jean-Bédel Bokassa crowned himself Emperor of Central Africa in Bangui, a year after renaming the Central African Republic an empire.

Modelled on Napoleon's coronation, the ceremony had a throne shaped like an eagle, a crown set with about two thousand diamonds and guests flown in from abroad, with help from France. It cost a large share of the yearly budget of one of the poorest countries in the world.

The empire lasted less than two years. It ended with Operation Barracuda in September 1979, when French troops flew in the former president Dacko and restored the republic in Bangui.
sum: On 4 December 1977 Jean-Bédel Bokassa crowned himself Emperor of Central Africa in Bangui, a year after renaming the Central African Republic an empire.
